explanation: The article gives the mechanism in one sentence: "Members of the Balkan League, seeing how easily Italy defeated the Ottomans and motivated by incipient Balkan nationalism, attacked the Ottoman Empire in October 1912, starting the First Balkan War a few days before the end of the Italo-Turkish War." Two things are named as what moved the League and only one of them is this war: what Italy supplied was the demonstration that the Ottoman army could be beaten, not the nationalism that wanted to beat it. A demonstration of weakness is a condition the later war was fought on and not the act that began it, so the weaker of the two types the source allows is the one written. The same lead calls the war "a precursor of World War I", which is a periodisation and not a mechanism, and no edge is written from it. Probable: Wikipedia alone, which rule 22 will not let stand as consensus.
